coverageNote.note: John Deere's FY2025 10-K lists 27 US/Canada factories + 12 distribution facilities; ~30 NA manufacturing/parts sites in audit scope. We audited 21. International scope on request.

account.dossierIntro: John Deere runs the largest heavy-equipment manufacturing network in the dataset. 60 facilities; we audited 21. Milan IL Parts Distribution covers 215 acres. Waterloo IA Tractor Operations is 620 acres. 3,914 total audited acres. YardFlow runs aftermarket parts logistics and whole-goods manufacturing as two distinct queues.
surprisingFindings: Waterloo IA is 620 acres of tractor manufacturing. Deere has been building Iowa-made tractors here since 1918.
Milan IL PDC is 215 acres with 90 dock doors. The largest aftermarket parts DC in agriculture.
3 of 21 audited sites are rail-served. Whole goods leave on flatbed; parts move on truckload.

sites.name: John Deere Waterloo Works - Tractor Operations - Waterloo IA
sites.dossierExcerpt:
Roster supplied geometric-center coordinates (42.522441, -92.269194) flagged as moved
2958 m. Satellite probe at z15-z16 landed directly on a massive industrial complex
surrounded entirely by farmland — unmistakably the John Deere Waterloo Works Tractor
Operations site (the largest Deere assembly complex in the world, building 7/8/9 Series
tractors). Web search confirmed 3500 E Donald St, Waterloo IA, with public 90-minute
riding factory tours. Center refined slightly SW to 42.5210, -92.2695 to sit on the
building mass.

fieldNotes.location: Confirmed flagship John Deere Waterloo Works Tractor Operations complex at 3500 E Donald St, Waterloo IA. Largest Deere assembly complex globally (7/8/9 Series tractors). Roster geometric-center coords (moved 2958m) landed on the building mass; locked center refined to 42.5210,-92.2695.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Inferred true with medium confidence. This is a Fortune-500 flagship assembly campus set far back from public roads behind long private internal drives; such plants are universally fenced and gate-controlled. Street View coverage stops at public rural roads (E Donald St / 41st St) and never reaches the actual truck gate, so the barrier arm could not be directly confirmed.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred true with medium confidence. A staffed guard post is standard for a plant of this scale running public riding-tours; not directly confirmed in imagery as SV cannot reach the internal gate.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Internal private drives from the SE road junction to the docks are very long (>1 km of approach) — easily holds a 3+ truck queue.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Central yard between building wings holds 60-90+ trailers in organized rows in the z18 imagery; capacity 50+.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated multi-row trailer storage lots visible between building wings (z18 view at 42.521,-92.2695).
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: Estimated 45 across multiple building faces from z18-z20 imagery; long building wings with trailers backed in on east and south faces. Approximate.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus with 6+ distinct building masses plus an on-site tractor test loop (42.517,-92.266) and two retention ponds.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock activity on physically separate building faces (north/east wings vs south wing staging) suggests separate ship/receive clusters; medium confidence.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide paved aprons and multi-lane internal drives provide ample room for express/bypass lanes.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Estimate; internal drives are wide multi-lane but exact gate lane count not visible.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale positively identified in imagery; left false, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Complex is surrounded entirely by farmland on the rural east edge of Waterloo IA — Rural.

citations.claim: Deere's official Waterloo factory page lists Tractor Operations among the five active Waterloo Works sites.
7/8/9 Series tractors including the new 9RX line are currently assembled in Waterloo.

verification.rationale: World's largest Deere tractor-assembly complex; new 9RX line confirms active production despite 2024-25 demand-driven layoffs.

sites.name: John Deere Waterloo Works - Engine Works - Waterloo IA

fieldNotes.truckGate: Inferred true, medium confidence. The whole property is clearly fenced (continuous fence line visible at z19-z20). The truck yard sits at the SE corner of the building accessed by a private driveway loop set well back from the road. Street View only reaches the surrounding public roads (W Ridgeway Ave north, side road east) and never reaches the truck-yard entrance, so a barrier arm could not be directly confirmed.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth positively identified. A small blue-roof structure at 42.4669,-92.4298 is a utility/pump building (set off in grass, away from the driveway pinch-point), not a guard shack. Set false; remoteGs set true accordingly.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: True by rule — gate inferred present but no guard shack visible, implying kiosk/call-box/app check-in.
fieldNotes.mainEntrance: Primary W Ridgeway Ave entrance is an open driveway leading to a circular visitor drive (flagpole) and employee parking — the office/visitor entrance, no gate.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: ~16 dock doors along the south building face; several blue/teal/green trailers backed in (z20 at 42.4678,-92.4318). Approximate.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Only a small number of trailers (~10-15) in the SE yard plus container/material-storage racks; band 0-10 for unaccompanied drop trailers, low confidence.
fieldNotes.dropYard: No dedicated multi-row trailer storage lot — yard is dock staging plus material racks; set false.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long private driveway loop from the road into the SE truck yard holds a 3+ truck queue.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved aprons and the deep driveway loop give ample room to add a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Main engine plant building plus a small ancillary structure; 2.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~95 acres including the large open grass land south of the building.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town Waterloo IA with cropland to the north and west and large open grass on the property — Rural.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Paved yard inside the fence before the docks; inferred true, low confidence.

citations.claim: Engine Works listed as one of the five active Waterloo Works sites on Deere's official locator.
Iowa DNR active permit record for John Deere Engine Works, 3801 W Ridgeway Ave, Waterloo, owned by Deere & Company.

verification.rationale: John Deere Power Systems diesel/natural-gas engine plant on Ridgeway Ave; active per Deere locator and Iowa DNR permit.

sites.name: John Deere Waterloo Works - Drivetrain Operations - Waterloo IA

The active production complex is enclosed by a continuous chain-link perimeter fence — clearly visible along the north road on multiple Street View headings (2026 imagery). fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth positively identified at a gate pinch-point. A small peaked-roof structure SE of the production building is a utility/maintenance building, not a guard shack. Set false; remoteGs true by rule.
fieldNotes.campus: Mixed-use campus — active Drivetrain Operations production buildings plus the John Deere Tractor & Engine Museum and TechWorks innovation campus on the south side. Significant building demolition visible (cleared foundations across the central/southern parcels).

fieldNotes.urbanRural: Within the urban fabric of Waterloo IA — residential neighborhood adjacent to the south, museum and business park on-campus, river and rail corridor — Urban.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus with 5+ distinct building masses (production buildings, museum, TechWorks).
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~110 acres bounded by the Cedar River (W), the north perimeter road, and Westfield Ave / the highway corridor (S).
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale identified; left false.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Paved yard inside the fence ahead of the docks; inferred true, low confidence.

citations.claim: Drivetrain Operations listed among the five active Waterloo Works sites on Deere's official factory page.
Iowa DNR active facility record for John Deere Waterloo Works - Drive Train Operations, 300 W Commercial St, Waterloo.

verification.rationale: Drivetrain (transmissions/axles) plant at 300 W Commercial St; active per Deere locator and DNR record.

sites.name: John Deere Waterloo Foundry - Waterloo IA

Waterloo Foundry at 2000 Westfield Ave. Locked center refined to 42.5072, -92.3650 on the

fieldNotes.location: Confirmed John Deere Waterloo Foundry at 2000 Westfield Ave, Waterloo IA. Roster ROOFTOP coords (moved 180m) landed on the large foundry building mass along the Cedar River; locked center refined to 42.5072,-92.3650.
fieldNotes.truckGate: CONFIRMED via Street View (2026 imagery, 42.5049,-92.3648). Multiple yellow barrier arms span the truck lanes, with a chain-link perimeter fence and gates. Definitive controlled truck entrance.
fieldNotes.guardShack: CONFIRMED. A brick gatehouse with a brown peaked-roof canopy sits directly beside the truck lanes between the inbound and outbound sides — a classic 1-3-vehicle-footprint staffed guard booth. Clearly visible in the 2026 Street View gate shots.
fieldNotes.railServed: TRUE. Rail tracks run alongside the foundry building between the building and the river levee, with spurs adjacent to the building (z18/z19 at 42.5085,-92.3645). Foundries typically receive scrap/pig iron by rail.

fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Deep paved approach from the gate to the dock building easily holds a 3+ truck queue.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide gate apron and multi-lane layout (lanes on both sides of the guard booth) — ample room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: ~20 dock doors across the foundry building's loading faces; a dock-door bank is visible in the SV east-facing gate shot. Approximate.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Few unaccompanied drop trailers observed (~8); the staging area is large but lightly used in the captured imagery. Band 0-10, medium confidence.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Large dedicated paved staging/trailer yard inside the gate; set true.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Within the industrial fabric of Waterloo IA — residential neighborhood adjacent to the SW, US-218 highway corridor, the broader Waterloo Works campus around it — Urban.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Multi-building foundry complex (4+ distinct large building masses) on one property.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Estimated 2 inbound / 2 outbound from the gate layout; exact count partly obscured.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale positively identified; left false, flagged uncertain.

citations.claim: Foundry Operations listed as one of the five active Waterloo Works sites.
Waterloo foundry currently casts gray/ductile iron components feeding tractor assembly.

verification.rationale: Active Deere-owned foundry (gray/ductile iron castings) feeding the Waterloo complex.

sites.name: John Deere Harvester Works - East Moline IL
sites.dossierExcerpt:
Roster supplied GEOMETRIC_CENTER coordinates (41.526702, -90.434909) flagged as moved
2007 m. Satellite probe landed directly on a massive industrial complex on the Mississippi
River. Web search confirmed the John Deere Harvester Works at 1100 13th Ave, East Moline
IL — the world's largest combine manufacturing facility (~4M sq ft, ~90 acres under roof),
producing combines since 1913. Google Maps place coordinates (41.5234, -90.4355)
corroborate. Locked center placed on the main building mass at 41.5240, -90.4360.

fieldNotes.location: Confirmed John Deere Harvester Works at 1100 13th Ave, East Moline IL — the world's largest combine manufacturing facility (~4M sq ft, ~90 acres under roof). Roster GEOMETRIC_CENTER coords (moved 2007m) landed on the complex; Google Maps place (41.5234,-90.4355) corroborates. Locked center placed on the main building mass at 41.5240,-90.4360.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Inferred true, medium confidence. Street View shows a 'John Deere Harvester Works Gate 12' sign at a private access drive — the plant uses a formal numbered-gate security system, with a continuous chain-link perimeter fence visible along 13th Ave. The actual gate barrier sits at the end of the private drive beyond Street View coverage.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred true, medium confidence. A flagship secured assembly plant with a numbered-gate system (Gate 12+) almost always staffs its gates; a guard booth could not be directly imaged because SV does not reach the gate itself.
fieldNotes.railServed: TRUE. Multiple rail tracks run through and alongside the plant buildings (z20 at 41.5245,-90.434 and 41.5243,-90.4338); rail tank/freight cars visible nearby. Harvester Works has long been rail-served.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive trailer drop yards — rows of trailers on the NW side plus trailer staging near the docks; 50+ band. Dozens of finished green combine harvesters also staged in the SE finished-goods yard.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Multiple dedicated trailer-storage lots (NW side rows of trailers) — set true.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: ~40 dock doors across multiple building faces with trailers backed in (z18-z20). Approximate.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Receiving docks (NW side, raw material / components by truck and rail) physically separate from the SE finished-goods staging/shipping yard — medium confidence.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus of 8+ distinct large building masses plus a visitor center.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long private access drives (e.g. the Gate 12 drive) hold a 3+ truck queue.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide gate aprons and multi-lane drives give room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: Multiple numbered gates serve the campus — separate in/out points likely.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Within the urban fabric of East Moline IL — dense residential neighborhoods directly adjacent on the SE; Quad Cities metro — Urban.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~410 acres bounded by the Mississippi River (NW) and 13th Ave / urban East Moline (SE).
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale positively identified; left false, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Estimated; exact gate lane counts not visible (SV does not reach the gates).

citations.claim: Deere's official locator confirms Harvester Works, East Moline IL is the active combine assembly plant.
$162M investment at Harvester Works and current X9 combine production.

verification.rationale: World's largest combine plant (~4M sqft); recent $162M reinvestment and X9 production confirm active operation.

sites.name: John Deere Davenport Works - Davenport IA

  point shows one enormous manufacturing complex standing alone in open

fieldNotes.truckGate: Site is set ~600 m back from the public road across landscaped grounds, reached by a wide private internal access road off a controlled intersection on E 90th St. Multi-lane markings at the road junction indicate a controlled private entry. fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth resolved at the public-road entry or along the access road in available imagery; large Deere assembly campuses of this era typically use a check-in point near the building rather than a road booth.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Set true as the corollary of an inferred gate with no resolved booth; low confidence.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Five distinct building masses on the campus: the giant main assembly hall plus older north/NE building sections and outbuildings.

fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Enormous paved aprons and wide internal roads leave abundant room for added or express truck lanes.

citations.claim: Davenport Works (2.2M sqft) has produced construction and forestry equipment since 1974; 6 active product lines.

fieldNotes.site: Resolved to the John Deere A&I Products complex in Rock Valley IA. A&I Products is John Deere's all-makes aftermarket-parts subsidiary (Deere acquired A&I in Dec 2010); Rock Valley is its corporate HQ, main manufacturing facility and central distribution hub - 750,000+ sq ft of warehouse space across roughly three connected/adjacent buildings. The roster address (1300 16th Ave) could not be confirmed; Waze lists 'John Deere A&I Products, 2200-2298 10th St' and Yelp lists 1020 22nd Ave for A&I HQ - both point to the same industrial-park complex SW of downtown Rock Valley, which is what was audited.
fieldNotes.coords: Locked center (43.19680, -96.31370) on the A&I warehouse/manufacturing complex. Roster coords (43.203456, -96.294498) plotted in downtown Rock Valley among small-town commercial/residential blocks and grain elevators - not the DC - and were not used.
fieldNotes.buildings: Approximately three large connected/adjacent warehouse + manufacturing buildings forming an L-shaped campus around a central courtyard apron. multipleFacilities = true. An XPO Logistics office sign is on one building's SE corner (XPO appears to provide 3PL services on site).
fieldNotes.truckGate: FALSE. Access is via an open road off 10th St running into the central courtyard. Four+ Street View captures from 2025-08, taken from inside the complex and along 10th St, show NO barrier arm, NO sliding/swing gate, and NO checkpoint pinch-point - the frontage is open with no perimeter fence.
fieldNotes.guardShack: FALSE. No staffed booth (1-3-vehicle footprint, multi-side windows) anywhere at or near the entrance in any Street View heading.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: FALSE. remoteGs requires a truck gate to exist; there is none.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: TRUE. The central courtyard between the buildings is a large paved apron that serves as internal staging for trucks before the dock / overhead doors.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: TRUE. The access road runs a long distance off 10th St into the courtyard - easily holds 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 10-25 band, MEDIUM/LOW confidence. The complex loads via a mix of dock-height doors and truck-level overhead drive-in doors facing the central courtyard and the access road. Street View confirms several dock and overhead positions; overhead imagery is consistent with roughly 12-20 doors. This is a manufacturing + distribution facility, not a high-bay cross-dock, so the count is moderate. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 0-10, LOW confidence. No large dedicated marked drop-trailer lot. A modest number of trailers park in the courtyard apron. dropYard = false. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropYard: FALSE. No dedicated trailer-storage lot full of parked trailers separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~8 trailers seen in/around the courtyard apron in the captured imagery; approximate, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: ~12, estimated courtyard apron capacity; low confidence.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: FALSE. Loading is concentrated around the central courtyard; no clearly separate ship vs receive dock banks on different building faces.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: TRUE. Single combined access road off 10th St; no separate in/out gates.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: FALSE. No gate exists and the entrance, while open, is a standard-width industrial access road - no obvious need or marked layout for an express bypass lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural. Rock Valley is a small town (~3,800 population) in NW Iowa; the complex sits in a small-town industrial park ringed by farmland - clearly Rural per the rubric's small-town guidance.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: FALSE (medium confidence). Although Rock Valley is small, the site is inside a built-up industrial park within the town, so cellular coverage is likely adequate. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: FALSE. No rail spur runs into the property.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~22 acres, derived from the perimeter box (~365 m N-S x ~245 m E-W of the owner-occupied A&I parcel). Estimate - the exact parcel boundary is not fenced/marked, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.scale: FALSE. No truck scale / weigh pad visible in the truck path.
fieldNotes.addressNote: Roster address 1300 16th Ave is unverified and likely incorrect; the audited complex is the John Deere A&I Products facility on 10th St / 22nd Ave in the SW Rock Valley industrial park.

citations.claim: Rock Valley IA is A&I Products' central distribution hub, HQ, and main manufacturing facility (all-makes aftermarket parts).
Deere completed full acquisition of A&I Products (Rock Valley IA); Deere spokesman confirms full ownership.

verification.rationale: Rock Valley 'All-Makes' PDC is A&I Products, a wholly Deere-owned subsidiary (sole owner since Jan 2011); Deere-operated all-makes parts distribution, currently active.
